findings.issue_text: Public group members page makes only one request and has no pagination, silently truncating groups with more than 50 members
group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer where an ActiveRecord association expects a User record, causing an association type mismatch instead of removing the member
totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, creating a nonexistent extra page when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit
Removing the only member on the last page reuses the stale offset, leaving the UI on an empty out-of-range page instead of adjusting the offset and refetching
The members API accepts limit and offset without bounds validation, allowing negative values that may cause database errors and arbitrarily large expensive queries
The group member template resolves automatic in the member context where it is absent, incorrectly showing removal links for automatic-group members

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page makes only one request and has no pagination, silently truncating groups with more than 50 members

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for the public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6), the setupController now calls model.findMembers() which uses a default limit of 50 (from group.js: limit: 50). The members endpoint in groups_controller.rb returns paginated results with limit/offset/total metadata. However, the group/members.hbs template just iterates over 'members' without any pagination controls (unlike the admin group page which has next/previous buttons). The public members page will only show the first 50 members with no way to see more, effectively truncating large groups silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer where an ActiveRecord association expects a User record, causing an association type mismatch instead of removing the member

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb, the remove_member method calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` where user_id is an integer from params. The ActiveRecord association's delete method expects either a User record or an array of User records, not an integer ID. This would cause the deletion to fail silently or raise an error. The correct approach would be to find the user first or use `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` or similar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The members API accepts limit and offset without bounds validation, allowing negative values that may cause database errors and arbitrarily large expensive queries

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in groups_controller.rb, the members action accepts limit and offset parameters: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`. While there's some validation in the JavaScript model (`offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`), the server-side controller has no bounds checking. A negative offset could cause database errors, and an arbitrarily large limit could cause expensive queries. The controller directly passes these values to the database query without validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The group member template resolves automatic in the member context where it is absent, incorrectly showing removal links for automatic-group members

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the group_member.hbs template: `{{#unless automatic}}{{fa-icon "times"}}{{/unless}}`. The template references `automatic` but is rendered in the context of a member (user), not the group. The `automatic` property exists on the group model, not on individual user/member objects. In the itemView context, `automatic` would be undefined/falsy on the member, so the `{{#unless automatic}}` check would always pass, showing the remove link even for automatic groups. The correct fix would be to reference the parent group's automatic property.
